description: Mechanical cross-check of contraction_intersections.md Part V: the exact cell-decomposition identity for two same-endpoint simple paths (non-crossing case), the explicit smallest counterexample disproving the 'canonical witnesses give exactly one cell' target, and the three resolved (non-crossing) named intersection-diagram types (common prefix, common suffix, enter-and-leave).
scope_note: Tests only the non-crossing case. The crossing case is explicitly left open in contraction_intersections.md V.3 (uncrossing is named as the standard technique but its hypotheses are not verified to hold in this project's setting); deliberately no gadget is built for it here, so as not to falsely validate an unresolved claim. Kept separate from the four prior contraction verifiers, none of which are touched.
note_on_python_version: Same environment note as prior manifests: requirements.txt/.python-version pin CPython 3.14.6, unavailable in this container; this run used 3.13.12 with networkx==3.6.1 (matches requirements.txt's pin exactly).

one_cell_target_disproof.interpretation: 0 shared edges and 0 common components (already minimal on the canonical-choice criteria) coexist with 2 divergent cells, not 1 -- direct disproof of the one-cell reduction target as stated.

detector_agreement: Every constructed gadget cycle validated by two independent implementations (hand-rolled adjacency traversal verify_cycle, and independently constructed networkx traversal verify_cycle_nx, both imported from verifier/contraction_lift.py); 0 disagreements.
completed_range: All gadget constructions processed to completion; this is a small, deterministic set of explicit illustrative constructions, not a search or census.
